text:
sec_alert_bot: 🚨 Detection alert: scanner found a possible live API key in a public CI log. Pattern matched 'rw_live_' in file infra/.github/workflows/build-8734.log. Creating thread for triage.

alex_g: On it — do we know which key type (hosted vs service account)?

maya_r: Looks like a hosted API key (rw_live_...). Snippet I pulled: ```...rw_live_abC1kZ9qfE...``` from https://github.com/redwood/infra/actions/runs/8734/logs.

john_ops: If it's hosted, we should revoke immediately. Any objections?

dana_infra: Hold up — quick check first: if it's used by infra-backup job we'll cause failures. I'll query audit logs for last usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://audit.redwood.internal/v1/events?query=api_key:rw_live_abC1kZ9qfE"`

maya_r: Ran the query. Last_request_ts=1915997500 from IP 35.207.12.9 to /v1/generate. Count=47 requests in last 24h. Looks active.

alex_g: OK revoke then rotate. I'll revoke and create a replacement. Command I will run: ```rwctl keys revoke --id rw_live_abC1kZ9qfE --reason "leak in public CI log"```

ops_bot: Revoke executed by alex_g at 1916001300. Result: SUCCESS. Old key disabled. New key created id=rw_live_newXYZ and stored in KMS path `projects/redwood/keys/infra-backup`. :white_check_mark:

john_ops: Confirm KMS RBAC — only infra-backup SA should have decrypt access. Dana, can you tighten IAM and enable key rotation?

dana_infra: On it. Updating KMS policy now. Command: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/infra-backup --member=serviceAccount:infra-backup@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` Removing old broad principals. Also enabling automatic rotation schedule (period=30d).

sarah_legal: Please collect request IDs, endpoints, and any associated customer IDs for the 47 requests. Legal needs to confirm whether customer data was accessed and whether notification is required. Tag me when you have the logs.

maya_r: I grepped the request logs and correlated user metadata. All 47 requests are from internal test projects (project_id=test-e2e-04, test-e2e-07). No production customer IDs found. I'll paste a redacted sample:
```
request_id: rq_34fa2
endpoint: /v1/generate
project_id: test-e2e-04
timestamp: 1915997402
```

alex_g: Good. Also: enable high-fidelity audit logging for that token and set retention to 90 days for post-incident analysis. I pushed a helper to ops to tag future leaked keys for retention.

maya_r: Created a short incident note in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/ci-api-key-leak-1916001234 (contains timeline + commands + logs).

sarah_legal: Based on the logs showing no customer data, legal recommends internal-only postmortem and no external customer notice. We'll prepare a one-paragraph summary for SOC/CISO.

john_ops: Action list (owner):
- Rotate any keys referenced in the repo (alex_g)
- Harden CI secret scanning to block commits with key patterns (alex_g + devex)
- Lock down KMS policies and enable rotation (dana_infra)
- Open monitoring ticket to detect leaked token usage anomalies (john_ops)
- Postmortem & runbook update (maya_r)

alex_g: I'll add a quick pre-commit check and CI linter rule to reject rw_live_ patterns and fail the build. Also adding a canary PR check to surface accidental check-ins.

dana_infra: IAM updated and rotation scheduled. Also removed old service account principals with overly broad access. Verified with `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy`.

ops_bot: Monitoring alert rule deployed: rule=leaked-key-usage, threshold=10 reqs/min for unknown IPs, notify=#eng-oncall.

maya_r: Small change to runbook: recommend storing runtime keys only in KMS and injecting them into CI via ephemeral secrets instead of committing to repo.

sarah_legal: I'll draft the internal notification and attach the legal signoff. No action needed for customers at this time.

john_ops: Filing tickets now: https://tickets.redwood.ai/browse/INF-8712 (CI scanning), INF-8713 (KMS RBAC), INF-8714 (postmortem). Assigning owners.

alex_g: Re-deployed infra-backup with new key and smoke-tested — OK. No job failures observed.

maya_r: Incident contained: leaked token revoked, replacement in KMS, IAM tightened, CI scanning rule in progress.

sec_alert_bot: Incident status: CONTAINED — token revoked at 1916001300. Post-incident follow-ups assigned. Closing this thread; postmortem ticket INC-2029-191600 (link: https://tickets.redwood.ai/INC-2029-191600).

john_ops: We'll reconvene in 1 hour to review the postmortem draft and ensure runbook updates are complete. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sarah_legal: Adding a quick note — keep the forensic artifacts for 180 days per compliance until signoff.

maya_r: Noted and stored artifacts in secure bucket `gs://sec-artifacts/1916001234/`.

alex_g: Closing my side: PR to add linter rule opened -> https://github.com/redwood/devex/pull/412 :rocket:

ops_bot: Automated verification: all jobs referencing old key now point to KMS path. verification_status=OK at 1916004567.
